transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, what brings me in is... I keep getting these really intense thoughts. I manage IT systems for a living, and I just have this constant fear that if I miss one setting, or one access rule, or a warning sign, someone could get hurt. Or they could lose everything. 

Part of me knows it’s irrational, but it hits me so hard, like I’m personally responsible if something goes wrong. I just can’t seem to let it go and move on. It's really starting to take a toll on me.
When these thoughts happen, do you find yourself doing certain things repeatedly, like checking your work over and over, to try to make the anxiety go away?

Yes, that's exactly what happens. I check things constantly. I’ll reread deployment plans, audit logs, even old messages, just over and over again. It is not just the digital stuff either, I do it with the physical door locks at work, too. 

Sometimes I find myself counting through the steps in my head while I check, and I have to keep doing it until it finally feels safe. It takes up so much time. I’ve actually stayed at the office for hours after everyone else has left, just checking things. If I try to force myself to stop before it feels complete... I just start to panic.

latest_inference.note: Patient confirms prominent, time-consuming compulsive rituals (repetitive checking, mental counting) performed to reduce distress caused by intrusive obsessive thoughts, with preserved insight. This confirms Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (F42) and rules out GAD (F41.1), OCPD (F60.5), and adjustment disorder (F43.2).

Persistent inflated sense of personal responsibility recognized as irrational

Panic and intense anxiety triggered by attempts to resist or stop rituals
